title: Etale scheme charts detect the local morphism properties of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fix one property $P$ from flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. On algebraic spaces these properties mean their extensions by etale scheme charts. Let $V\to Y$ be a surjective etale morphism from a scheme, and let $U\to X\times_YV$ be a surjective etale morphism from a scheme [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Then $f$ has $P$ if and only if the scheme morphism $U\to V$ has $P$. The criterion holds for every such pair of charts, including $V=Y$ when $Y$ is a scheme. If $X$ and $Y$ are schemes, the extended property agrees with the indicated scheme property. No quasi-compactness, separation, or other one of the three properties is assumed.

proof.text: Fix the indicated scheme property $P$. By [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties], each of flatness, local finite presentation and local finite type is etale local on source-and-target. Thus $P$ satisfies the hypothesis of the algebraic-space presentation criterion; we use its chart extension, defined by requiring $P$ on every etale scheme presentation diagram. No implication between the three properties is used. These properties are invariant under scheme isomorphisms: the defining local rings, affine opens and finite algebra presentations are carried to isomorphic ones [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

Put $Z=X\times_YV$, let $p:Z\to X$ be the projection, and write $q:U\to Z$ for the given chart and $h:U\to V$ for the composite $U\to Z\to V$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $Z$ is an algebraic space and the sheaf fibre product of $f$ and $b:V\to Y$, so $p$ is the base change of $b$ along $f$. By [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], representable surjective etale morphisms are stable under arbitrary algebraic-space base change and under composition, and $q$, a surjective etale map from a scheme, is representable surjective etale. Hence $p$ and then $a=pq:U\to X$ are representable surjective etale. The fibre-product square gives $fa=bh$, where $b$ is the given representable etale map. Thus $(a,b,h)$ is a presentation diagram with surjective source chart.

source.place: Tag 03MJ (lemma-local-source-target), diagrams; spaces.tex Tag 02X2 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces), Tags 02WK (lemma-composition-representable-transformations-property) and 02WL (lemma-base-change-representable-transformations-property) for etale and surjective.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] to $P$ and the diagram of Step 2. Its conditions (1) and (2) are equivalent: the universal chart test defining $P(f)$ implies $P(h)$ for this diagram, and conversely $P(h)$ in this one diagram, whose source chart $a$ is surjective, implies the universal chart test. Consequently $P(f)\Longleftrightarrow P(U\to V)$.

source.place: Tag 03MJ (lemma-local-source-target), equivalence (1) and (2), and definition-P; Tags 03MM (lemma-flat-local), 0410 (lemma-finite-presentation-local), 040Y (lemma-finite-type-local), conditions (7),(8).

proof.text: The pair of charts in Steps 2--3 was arbitrary, so the equivalence holds for every such pair. If $Y$ is a scheme, the identity $Y\to Y$ is an isomorphism, hence representable surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], so it is an allowed target chart, and then $X\times_YY=X$. If both $X$ and $Y$ are schemes, the final scheme-comparison clause of [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] identifies the universal chart extension with the original scheme property. All inputs apply without quasi-compactness or separation hypotheses.

So p = base change of b along f, then a = pq, is representable surjective etale; the identity Y->Y works when Y is a scheme. proof_deps and split_report.tool_uses are updated to match. lean.statement: theorem local_properties_chart_test {S : Scheme.{u}} (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) (hP : P = @Flat ∨ P = @LocallyOfFinitePresentation ∨ P = @LocallyOfFiniteType) {X Y : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (V : Over S) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y.obj.obj) (hb : IsEtale b) (hbs : IsSurjective b) (U : Over S) (q : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Limits.pullback f.hom.hom b) (hq : IsEtale q) (hqs : IsSurjective q) : MapIsLocally P f ↔ P (yoneda.preimage (q ≫ Limits.pullback.snd f.hom.hom b)).left
lean.note: The main theorem states the arbitrary surjective etale pullback-chart test for exactly the three named properties. The second theorem gives agreement of the universal chart extension with the scheme property. Reuses MapIsLocally and EtalePresentation from the recorded dependencies; no additional locality or isomorphism-invariance hypothesis is imposed.
